title: Breadth-first search program
statement: For each natural number $K_0$, define a program for a nondeterministic finite Turing machine on binary inputs. Its labels implement the following stages: query the input-length decider while counting the input length and computing its logarithmic scale; initialize the search width; perform two searches using the initial-code and step deciders, relaxing marks and counting marked codes; compare the counts; and then scan for an accepting code, halting with acceptance or rejection. The program uses copy routines, a counter-transfer routine, shifts of the search bound, and memory-access routines to carry out these stages.
caveat: The declaration is a large case-defined program; this high-level description omits the individual label-to-instruction assignments.
